newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Preussag to hike oil output in Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: Preussag to hike oil output in Venezuela.

text.p: German industrial giant Preussag plans to increase production in Venezuela's Cabimas oilfield from 3,500 barrels per day (bpd) to 12,000 bpd by 2000, a company official said Thursday.
Preussag won a contract to exploit the field for 20 years on behalf of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela with a bid of $500,000 in Venezuela's third round of operating licences.
It was the only bid for the field which is located in Cabimas town on the edge of Lake Maracaibo in western Venezuela.
Preussag Americas president Rudolph Berends said the company planned to drill 17 wells as part of its reactivation programme, and that 12,000 bpd was only a preliminary estimate of planned .
He declined to specify how much the company planned to spend on the field, but said it would be well in excess of the $40 million minimum required by the contract.
The field currently has 28 million barrels of proven reserves, but the company planned to increase this figure in the course of its work.

According to the contract, Preussag will receive a fee based on a complex formula which participants say offers the contractor the chance to recoup their investment by raising production and then get 30 percent of the profits from any additional output, up to a pre-set ceiling.
Preussag's existing Latin American oil interests include contracts in Argentina, Colombia and Ecuador.
